A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same anatomical-prior segmentation work, renamed from AIC-UNet to AIC-Net. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original WORD segmentation experiments comparing AIC-UNet, CUNet and UNet in Table 1, alongside learned-prior visualizations and qualitative predictions.

after.justification: v2 reports original TotalSegmentator organ and vertebra experiments across four backbones, component analyses, and class-level results in appendix Tables 3–10.

M1.justification: The global-local cascade and alternating prior optimization remain, but v2 adds per-organ affine translations before TPS, centroid alignment loss, and residual SE fusion with layer normalization. The documented objective changes from combined Soft-Dice and cross-entropy with TPS regularization to Soft-Dice, centroid loss and regularization. These change the procedure beyond renaming.

E1.justification: The WORD evaluation covering 16 abdominal structures is replaced by TotalSegmentator organ and vertebra tasks. The later evaluation includes vertebral identity prediction and additional structures such as lung lobes, thyroid and prostate, with varied scan coverage. WORD results are not retained.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates UNet and cascaded UNet comparators. v2 retains the vanilla/cascaded comparison structure and adds evaluated DeepLabV3+, UNETR and UNETR-Swin comparators, each in vanilla and cascaded forms, as shown in Table 1.

E3.justification: The stated training budget changes from 350 epochs of 200 iterations to 200,000 iterations, and TPS regularization weights change from 1e-8 to 1e-5. v2 specifies centroid-loss weights of 0.5 and a vertebra intensity window of [-250, 1100]. Its new dataset uses a 1082/57/65 training/validation/test split instead of WORD's 100/20/30. Dice, NSD and HD95 remain the evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: v2 adds a with/without-centroid-loss analysis of malformed vertebral priors under different scan coverage (Figure 4), and measures local-prior accuracy before and after deformation across backbones and tasks (Table 2). The earlier femur and gallbladder cases are replaced by vertebral-label, spleen and adrenal cases. These provide new component and failure analyses.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates only. v2 adds mean-plus-standard-deviation reporting throughout appendix Tables 3–10. This is a descriptive reporting addition; neither version documents repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v2 does not clearly specify the standard-deviation aggregation procedure.

E6.justification: The WORD results are replaced by TotalSegmentator aggregate and class-level results, with additional component findings. For example, v2 Table 1 reports vertebra HD95 of 12.6 versus 52.2 for AIC-Net versus vanilla UNETR, but vertebra Dice of 89.3 versus 90.2 for AIC-Net versus vanilla UNETR-Swin. These are new-setting comparisons, not v1-to-v2 performance gains. Table 7's organ mean row also conflicts with Table 1 and repeats the vertebra means.

T1.justification: v2 introduces formal centroid and centroid-loss definitions and a revised composite objective. The appendix also substantively corrects TPS interpolation: its kernel and polynomial matrices use target control points, while the right-hand side uses source coordinates; v1 used source coordinates in both. This changes the mathematical construction rather than merely its notation.

C1.justification: The anatomical-prior and global-local contributions remain, but v2 replaces the advertised activation-maximization contribution with a novel centroid-loss contribution and explicitly includes affine-plus-TPS alignment. Its abstract and introduction assert performance improvements across multiple backbones and two tasks. The general applicability claim itself already existed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of flat deformation-loss regions and how centroid alignment addresses them, interprets HD95 as an anatomical-accuracy indicator, and discusses vertebral-label guidance. It newly acknowledges doubled model size and memory consumption, limited fine-detail deformation, and failure to predict kidney cyst classes. These substantially extend v1's optimization hypothesis and brief future-work discussion.

D1.justification: v2 adds implementation information about affine/TPS prediction heads, trilinear resampling, fixed target points and precomputed TPS inversion, the padded volume size, and sliding-window inference. These are documentation additions where v1 did not specify the corresponding details. Conversely, v1's code-availability statement and URL disappear; the PDFs do not establish whether the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around template and atlas methods, multiclass topology losses, and limitations of transformers with limited data. Added references include TETRIS, Bayesian atlas approaches, Mamba/Mamba-UNet and recent validation studies. The earlier GNN discussion and its citations are removed, changing the surrounding research context.

P1.justification: Beyond the new title and AIC-Net terminology, v2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion. It reorganizes the method into more detailed component and loss subsections and develops a Results and Discussion narrative. This is substantial rewriting alongside the scientific additions.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column to a two-column layout. The architecture and deformation diagrams are redrawn and combined, a separate SE-res diagram and centroid-loss figure are added, and qualitative displays are replaced or expanded. The compact WORD table is replaced by a multi-backbone summary, a deformation table and eight appendix result tables.

improvement.justification: The four-backbone, two-task evaluation and direct centroid/deformation analyses substantially strengthen validation beyond v1's single-backbone WORD study. The corrected TPS construction and explicit resource and failure limitations also improve technical clarity. These gains outweigh material reporting weaknesses: the code pointer disappears, Table 1 contradicts blanket superiority claims, and Table 7's organ means repeat vertebra results. Those flaws qualify the conclusions but do not erase the substantial improvement in evidence and explanation.
